To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the performance of the CAC algorithm depends on the traffic class, (2) the performance of CAC for the NS-VBR traffic class depends on the channel capacity, and (3) the performance of both CAC for NS-VBR and CAC for S-VBR depends on the busy period length T.

1) the performability of a CAC algorithm can be very sensitive to the traffic class (NS-VBR or S-VBR) and to the value of T; 2) the performability is also very sensitive to the channel capacity fluctuation rate; and 3) the performability may be significantly different from what is predicted by a simple approximation based on a single worst-case scenario.

(1) CAC algorithms based on effective bandwidth calculations are capable of providing a high level of performance and (2) the level of performance is sensitive to the assumptions made in the effective bandwidth calculation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performability of CAC algorithms that accommodate variable bit-rate (VBR) sources and are based on the effective bandwidth concept.
developing a framework for performability analysis of CAC algorithms for ATM networks.
the development of a performability framework for evaluating the performance and reliability of CAC algorithms in ATM networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the performance of the algorithms considered is very much dependent on the traffic mix, and that the performance of all algorithms is sensitive to the channel capacity fluctuations, especially for the NS-VBR class.
the performance of all algorithms considered in this paper deteriorate significantly when the traffic is not S-VBR.
the CAC algorithms are quite sensitive to channel capacity fluctuations and that S-VBR traffic is more sensitive than NS-VBR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the presence of channel fluctuations, performability of CAC algorithms is highly dependent upon traffic type, traffic load, channel fluctuation, and the algorithm's ability to adapt to changing conditions.

the CAC algorithm that is based on the worst-case effective bandwidth of the S-VBR traffic class is the best performer, while the algorithm based on the worst case effective bandwidth of the NS-VBR traffic class performs the worst.
the performability models constructed and solved using the UltraSAN software package are very effective in evaluating the performance of CAC algorithms in a variety of scenarios.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performability of CAC algorithms can be quite sensitive to the traffic classes that are allowed to benefit from statistical multipexing.
the ability of a CAC algorithm to perform is highly dependent on the nature of the traffic classes it must accommodate, the channel capacity it must work with, and the busy period T.

the ability of CAC algorithms to accommodate fluctuating channel capacity can be assessed by performability analysis, which is a powerful technique for the analysis of stochastic, discrete event dynamic systems.
